newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-ENQVIST CLOSES IN ON SECOND STRAIGHT TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ENQVIST CLOSES IN ON SECOND STRAIGHT TITLE.

text.p: Sweden's Thomas Enqvist moved to within one match of clinching successive titles when he battled to a three-set victory over compatriot Thomas Johansson at the Stockholm Open on Saturday.
Enqvist, who has finished the season on a high note after clinching the Paris Open last week and this week's unbeaten run, conceded his first set in the tournament in beating Johansson 6-3 3-6 6-3.
The 22-year-old Swede, the third seed, will meet American Todd Martin, with the winner also booking the reserve place for the ATP World Championship later this month.

Martin enjoyed an easier day's work, advancing when his opponent, Swedish wild card Magnus Norman, was forced to retire due to an ankle injury. The second-seeded American was leading 6-3 3-0 at the time.
The two finalists are battling for a reserve place at the year-ending championship, reserved for the world's top eight players, starting in Hanover on November 19.
ATP spokesman Benito Perez-Barbadillo said the winner of Sunday's match would play in Hanover should any of the eight players selected withdraw from the championship.
